「興味を持つ」を分解する――interest is a chain, not a switch

To say we 'have an interest' makes interest sound like one thing inside a person. This essay decomposes it into a chain: attention stops, a discrepancy appears, the object feels understandable, a knowledge gap gets a contour, personal value emerges, and re-engagement begins. Drawing on psychology, education research, and neuroscience, it reframes interest not as a fixed taste but as a relation that develops between a person and an object.
